added.title: DevOps Engineer
added.description:
Responsibilities

During your shift, execute scheduled ServiceNow change tasks (CTASKs) and maintenance windows in accordance with approved change plans and runbooks.
Install security patches and renew certificates during their scheduled change windows.
After applying each change, verify it, roll it back if it fails, and document the result in ServiceNow.
Monitor dashboards and alerts throughout your shift. Respond by determining whether an alert is genuine, resolving routine issues using the runbook, and escalating anything else.
Serve as the first responder for incidents while the US team is offline. If a runbook does not cover the problem, escalate it to the Deployments lead or the DevOps Lead.
Maintain accurate runbooks by correcting or adding steps that are wrong or missing after each change or incident.
Conduct live handoffs at the beginning and end of every shift, and leave written notes about open work, incidents, and anything the next shift needs to monitor.
Contribute to the team's coverage metrics, including changes completed on schedule and changes delayed or rolled back.

Tools and environments

For change management, use ServiceNow
change tasks (CTASKs) and change approval records.
For automation, use Ansible on Linux servers
running primarily Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL).
Monitoring and observability tools include Grafana dashboards, Monit, centralized log aggregation, and Java Melody
for Java application performance.
Environments include application environments on cruise ships and in shore data centers across multiple time zones. Ship environments may have limited, high-latency satellite connectivity.
Production and ship system access is granted after onboarding and security approval [TBD: VPN, remote access and approval process].
